summary: SAML AuthnInstant timezone-offset parse mismatch intermittently causes 403s for tenant export workers (private)
description:
Issue summary:

Customer (Nimbus Health) reports intermittent 403s for their scheduled export workers that run in the private VPC deployment. The failures started after an identity provider rotation on 2025-02-10 and affect long-running scheduled batch jobs that use SAML->session assertions created by the customer IdP.

Impact:
- Several nightly export jobs fail ~10-20% of runs across 3 tenants; when they fail the worker reports 403 from Redwood admin API token-swap endpoint.
- Customer visibility: export backfill delays; operational impact to downstream analytics pipeline.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) in eu-west region behind customer edge proxy.
- IdP: Customer-hosted SAML IdP (Shibboleth) with per-tenant metadata and rotating signing keys.
- Affected components: identity-proxy token-exchange path, session assertion ingestion, scheduled-worker token refresh flow.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) IdP rotates signing keys (metadata updated) and publishes new SAML assertions for service account login.
2) Scheduled worker obtains SAML assertion and posts to Redwood identity-proxy /assertion endpoint to exchange for session tokens.
3) Approximately 1 in 8 exchanges return 403 (unauthorized) with body: "authorization failed: assertion validation error: authnInstant mismatch".

Observed logs (customer and Redwood):
- identity-proxy logs (excerpt): 
  "2025-02-11T02:14:12Z WARN assertion-validate tenant=nh-prod svc=scheduled-worker err=\"authnInstant parse error: invalid timezone offset\""
- token-swap endpoint returns 403 with structured error code AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FAIL.
- No 5xx from upstream, no network errors reported.

Workaround reported by customer:
- Re-running the job after 30-60s succeeds in most cases.
- Temporary mitigation: customer disabled clock-skew strict validation on their IdP (not ideal).

Desired outcome:
- Determine root cause and provide a fix or recommended remediation for the customer's private deployment.
- Provide a non-invasive mitigation that does not require disabling IdP validation or manual retries for every job.
comments: 2025-02-11 09:12 - Support (Avery Chen): Acknowledged. Gathering logs and escalated to SRE. SLA P1 acknowledged. Working with customer to capture a full SAML assertion sample (redacted).

2025-02-11 11:03 - Customer (Helena Ortiz, Nimbus Health): We captured three failing assertions and attached them to the secure file share. Failures mostly occur in exporters scheduled between 02:00-03:30 UTC. No other services reported issues.

2025-02-11 13:22 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Initial triage: parity check between identity-proxy SAML parser and upstream library (python-saml) shows we reject timezone offsets with colon vs no-colon variants in offset part (e.g., +01:00 vs +0100) depending on incoming assertion format. We requested the actual Assertion XML from customer to confirm.

2025-02-12 08:45 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Confirmed failing assertions contain authnInstant="2025-02-11T02:12:34+01:00" while our parser path normalizes tz to +0100. Edge case occurs when IdP sends fractional seconds or the colon in offset is present; parser rejects when fractional seconds are present with colon. Working on a reproduction test harness.

2025-02-12 14:05 - Support (Avery Chen): Customer applied a short-term retry backoff in their scheduled worker and reports success rate improved to 98%. Requested permission to enable a permissive parsing fallback in identity-proxy for their private deployment as a hotfix.

2025-02-13 09:02 - Engineering (Sofia Rivera): Agreed to a targeted fallback. Will ship an opt-in config to the customer's control plane that enables relaxed SAML datetime parsing. Preparing patch and integration test to ensure strict mode remains default.
2025-02-13 12:30 - Customer (Helena Ortiz): Approved opt-in hotfix for relaxed parsing while upstream IdP team adjusts assertion generation. Please provide rollback steps.

2025-02-13 16:40 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Hotfix deployed to customer's private control plane: identity-proxy config flag 'saml_datetime_permissive=true'. Monitoring for 24h. Rollback: toggle flag to false and restart identity-proxy; documented in deployment notes.
investigation_notes: 1) Collected three failing Assertion XML payloads from customer; samples show authnInstant variants: with and without fractional seconds, with timezone offsets both in +HH:MM and +HHMM formats.

2) Reproduced parsing failure in unit test where authnInstant contained fractional seconds plus colon-based offset: our parser's regex expects either fractional seconds OR coloned offset, not both (legacy regex bug introduced in 2023 datetime refactor).

3) Hypothesis: IdP rotation triggered a minor change in assertion formatting (new IdP version returned timestamps with fractional seconds and coloned offsets). Because assertions are otherwise valid and signed, failures appear intermittent depending on which IdP node served the assertion (mix of old/new formatting during rotation).

4) Confirmed that strict validation path returns AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FAIL before signature validation, therefore re-signing assertions won't help if parser rejects format.
Test harness: identity-proxy unit tests created with sample assertions; local runs show 1 failure pattern identical to customer.

5) Compatibility options explored: update regex to accept both formats, or add a permissive parsing path that normalizes datetime into RFC3339 canonical form before downstream validation. Chosen approach: permissive normalization with feature flag to avoid global behavior change.

6) Related risk: permissive parsing could mask malformed assertions. Mitigation: keep permissive mode opt-in per-customer; add additional assertion syntactic checks and log-level increase for discreet monitoring.
resolution:
Hotfix: deployed opt-in identity-proxy configuration 'saml_datetime_permissive=true' to Nimbus Health private control plane on 2025-02-13 16:40 UTC. The permissive path normalizes authnInstant variants (handles fractional seconds and both +HH:MM and +HHMM offsets) and falls back to strict parsing for malformed values. Post-deployment monitoring (24h) shows failure rate dropped from ~12% to <1% for scheduled exporters.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering will submit upstream patch to identity-proxy master to include normalized parsing + unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412). Target merge after security review.
- Ops: Provide a runbook entry for toggling 'saml_datetime_permissive' and guidance for customers during IdP rotations.
- Product/Security: Evaluate if permissive mode requires explicit customer acknowledgement as a documented compatibility tradeoff.

Status: Pending PR merge and post-24h monitoring completion. Customer accepted hotfix and will coordinate IdP patch rollout to remove the need for permissive mode.
notes_for_followup: - Ensure unit tests cover authnInstant formats with fractional seconds and both offset styles.
- Add telemetry metric AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FALLBACK_COUNT per tenant to detect other customers who may benefit or be at risk.
- Draft customer-facing KB article describing the issue, safe workarounds, and steps to harden IdP assertion formatting.
